bug_description.normalized:
The staged 42-byte witness `ff ff ff ff ff ff 20 20 5b 5d 5b 5b 21 5b 24 7c 24 5d 28 29 5d 5d 0a 0a 5b ff 5d 3a ff 0a 5b 5b 21 5b 7c 5d 28 29 5d 5d 5b 5d` makes `fuzz-mdhtml` pass `parser_flags == 0xffffffff`, `renderer_flags == 0x2020ffff`, and the 34-byte Markdown payload `[][[![$|$]()]]

[\xff]:\xff
[[![|]()]][]` into `md_parse()`. Because all parser-flag bits are set, `md_build_mark_char_map()` treats `|` as a significant inline mark. The block starting with `[\xff]:\xff` becomes one stored reference definition and later one-entry reference-definition hash table. When `md_process_all_blocks()` renders the earlier paragraph `[][[![$|$]()]]`, wiki-link resolution splits the construct at its `|` delimiter and `md_rollback()` requeues the crossing image opener onto `TABLECELLBOUNDARIES`, leaving chain 1 live at mark slot 10. The vulnerable generic chain-reset loops still start at `OPENERS_CHAIN_FIRST == 2`, so chain 1 survives the end of that paragraph. When the later block `[[![|]()]][]` reuses `ctx->marks`, stale chain slot 10 is recycled as that block's current `]` mark; the later wiki-link rollback on delimiter slot 9 then appends current opener slot 6 through the stale chain, overwriting `marks[10].next = 6` and `marks[6].prev = 10` while clearing mark 10's resolved-closer bits. The collapsed-reference call at `md_resolve_links()` is then driven by corrupted mark bookkeeping rather than a real `[label]` pair. `md_is_link_reference()` derives `label_size = end - beg` from that malformed range; because `MD_SIZE`/`MD_OFFSET` are unsigned, that width wraps to a huge value. `md_lookup_ref_def()` hashes the malformed label with `md_link_label_hash()`, which walks forward until `md_decode_utf8__()` reads one byte past the end of honggfuzz's 1 MiB input buffer. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow read at `src/md4c.c:817` in stack `md_decode_utf8__ -> md_link_label_hash -> md_is_link_reference`, and the staged fix removes the stale-chain carryover by resetting chain 1 together with the ordinary opener chains (`OPENERS_CHAIN_FIRST` from 2 to 1).

evidence_note: `trace_feedback.json` required repairing the later-block stale-chain mutation. `run_flags.json` keeps `runtime_disambiguation` disabled, so this pass stayed fully source-grounded and did not instrument or rerun the workspace. The saved ASan trace, staged PoC bytes, vulnerable source, and staged fix diff were sufficient to rebuild the stale-chain carryover, the later-block mark corruption, and the unchecked unsigned-width path in `md_is_link_reference()`, but they do not identify the exact unresolved-link node that reaches `src/md4c.c:3615`.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that materializes the parser-visible Markdown slice and parser flags. On this path those flags later enable wiki-link and `|` mark handling.
source.value_from:
The staged PoC at `gt_results/arvo_43589/poc` has sha256 `85d36b2ffe5eafb187c181b61f9fb34af85190fbcf301b19a97f284dc5f69c45` and exact bytes `ff ff ff ff ff ff 20 20 5b 5d 5b 5b 21 5b 24 7c 24 5d 28 29 5d 5d 0a 0a 5b ff 5d 3a ff 0a 5b 5b 21 5b 7c 5d 28 29 5d 5d 5b 5d`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` reads the first 4 bytes as `parser_flags == 0xffffffff`, the next 4 bytes as `renderer_flags == 0x2020ffff`, and passes the remaining 34-byte payload `[][[![$|$]()]]

[\xff]:\xff
[[![|]()]][]` to `md_html()` / `md_parse()`. Because all parser-flag bits are set, the vulnerable path has `MD_FLAG_WIKILINKS` enabled when the Markdown payload is parsed.

root_cause.description: After wiki-link rollback can populate `TABLECELLBOUNDARIES` (chain 1), this reset loop still starts at `OPENERS_CHAIN_FIRST == 2`, so chain 1 survives across blocks even though `ctx->marks` will be reused. The patch fixes this exact obligation by changing `OPENERS_CHAIN_FIRST` from 2 to 1 so chain 1 is reset with the ordinary opener chains.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `md_decode_utf8__()` unconditionally reads `str[0]`; after the malformed label hash has advanced `off` to the end of honggfuzz's 1 MiB input buffer, this dereferences the first byte beyond that allocation.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/md4c.c:817:13` on an address 0 bytes to the right of a 1048576-byte region, with stack `md_decode_utf8__ -> md_decode_unicode -> md_link_label_hash -> md_lookup_ref_def -> md_is_link_reference -> md_resolve_links`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is the first project-code point where attacker-controlled bytes become parser state: the Markdown slice itself and the parser flags that later enable special `|` handling.

parser_admitted.description: After block analysis has already consumed `[\xff]:\xff` as a reference definition and preserved `[[![|]()]][]` as the remaining paragraph text, the normal-block inline parser is invoked on that later block.

coarse_trace.summary: The honggfuzz harness consumes the first 8 testcase bytes as `parser_flags` and `renderer_flags`, then passes the remaining 34-byte Markdown payload into `md_html()` / `md_parse()`.
md4c stores the parser-visible text span and parser flags, then enables `|` as a significant mark character because wiki-links are enabled on the crashing path.
The block beginning with `[\xff]:\xff` is stored as one reference definition, and `md_build_ref_def_hashtable()` later makes reference-label hashing active for subsequent lookups.

While rendering the earlier paragraph `[][[![$|$]()]]`, wiki-link rollback around the `|` delimiter requeues crossing state onto `TABLECELLBOUNDARIES`; the vulnerable chain-reset logic leaves that chain live after the block ends.

The later paragraph `[[![|]()]][]` reuses `ctx->marks`; stale chain 1 now aliases current slot 10, and the second wiki-link rollback appends current opener slot 6 through that stale chain, overwriting current mark links before collapsed reference-link resolution.

The saved ASan stack shows the corrupted later-block mark state reaches the collapsed-reference path in `md_is_link_reference()`, whose unchecked unsigned `label_size = end - beg` can wrap huge; hashing that oversized label walks to the end of honggfuzz's 1 MiB input buffer and crashes in `md_decode_utf8__()`.

fine_trace.note:
Stores the parser-visible Markdown slice and parser flags. For the staged witness, `ctx.text` points at the 34-byte payload `[][[![$|$]()]]

[\xff]:\xff
[[![|]()]][]`, `ctx.size == 34`, and `ctx.parser.flags == 0xffffffff`, which includes the wiki-link extension needed on the crashing path.

Because the attacker-controlled parser flags have `MD_FLAG_WIKILINKS` set, md4c treats `|` as a significant inline mark. That allows the `|` bytes inside the payload's wiki-link-like constructs to become first-class marks later in inline analysis.

The block line `[\xff]:\xff` is recognized as one reference definition. md4c stores its single-byte label `0xff`, destination `0xff`, and increments `ctx->n_ref_defs` to 1, which is necessary for later reference lookups to do real hashing work instead of returning at the empty-table fast path.

After block analysis, md4c builds the reference-definition hashtable. With exactly one stored definition, `ctx->ref_def_hashtable_size` becomes nonzero, so later `md_lookup_ref_def()` calls must hash candidate labels and cannot short-circuit at `if(ctx->ref_def_hashtable_size == 0)`.

While scanning the first paragraph `[][[![$|$]()]]`, md4c materializes the `|` inside `[[![$|$]()]]` as a mark because wiki-link handling is enabled. That mark becomes the delimiter `delim` used by later wiki-link rollback.

The first paragraph's wiki-link-like construct has a real delimiter and nonempty text after it, so md4c splits it at `|` and rolls back the destination and label separately. In `[[![$|$]()]]`, the image opener `![` begins before the delimiter while its `]` closer is after it, so the second rollback must handle a crossing opener/closer pair.

During the second rollback, `opener_index` is the `|` delimiter mark. `md_mark_chain()` maps `|` to `TABLECELLBOUNDARIES`, so the crossing opener from `![$|$]()` is requeued onto chain 1 instead of being forgotten. That makes `TABLECELLBOUNDARIES` live even though no real table parsing is in progress.

Root cause. After step 7 has populated `TABLECELLBOUNDARIES`, this generic reset still starts at `OPENERS_CHAIN_FIRST == 2`, so chain 1 survives the end of the first paragraph. The fix commit changes that macro to 1 so this loop also clears `TABLECELLBOUNDARIES`.

When md4c starts inline analysis of the later block `[[![|]()]][]`, it reuses `ctx->marks` from index 0 by resetting only `ctx->n_marks`. The new marks occupy slots 0..16, including slot 6 for the current `![`, slot 9 for the current `|`, slot 10 for the current `]` at offsets 27..28, and slots 13/16 for the trailing `[]`. Because step 8 left `TABLECELLBOUNDARIES` intact with head/tail still equal to 10, chain 1 now aliases that recycled current slot 10.

Before the outer wiki-link rollback runs on `[[![|]()]]`, `md_resolve_links()` resolves the inner `![|]()` as an inline image. In the current recycled mark array that makes slot 6 the resolved opener and slot 10 the resolved closer, with `marks[10].prev = 6` and `marks[10].end = 30` after the empty `()` destination is eaten.

When the outer wiki-link `[[![|]()]]` is split at delimiter slot 9, `md_rollback(ctx, 9, 11, MD_ROLLBACK_CROSSING)` revisits current slot 10 as a resolved closer whose opener is slot 6. `md_mark_chain(ctx, 9)` returns stale chain 1, whose head/tail still alias current slot 10 from step 9, so `md_mark_chain_append()` writes `marks[10].next = 6` and `marks[6].prev = 10`. `discard_flag` then clears slot 10's `MD_MARK_CLOSER|MD_MARK_RESOLVED` bits but leaves its `beg = 27` and widened `end = 30`. This is the missing second-block corruption of current mark bookkeeping.

depends_on.via: stale TABLECELLBOUNDARIES head/tail = 10 and delimiter slot 9

fine_trace.note: The saved ASan stack proves a later unresolved-link iteration reaches this collapsed-reference call at line 3615. The vulnerable source passes `opener->beg` and `closer->end` straight from the current unresolved bracket candidate into `md_is_link_reference()` and only gates on `!(opener->flags & MD_MARK_HASNESTEDBRACKETS)`. After step 11, current mark bookkeeping is inconsistent: stale chain 1 still threads through current slots 10 and 6 even though slot 10 is no longer a resolved closer. Source-only artifacts do not identify which unresolved-link node hits line 3615, so this trace does not claim a specific `opener/closer` index pair.

No non-assert guard checks that `beg < end`. Once step 12 passes a malformed current-state range into this helper, `beg += ...`, `end--`, and the unsigned `label_size = end - beg` computation can wrap to a huge value instead of staying within the short single-line span. The saved end-of-buffer ASan read forces that oversized-label path to occur on this witness.

Because step 4 built a nonempty reference-definition table, the malformed label from step 13 reaches `md_link_label_hash()` instead of returning immediately. That is the gate that puts the oversized `label_size` onto the crashing hashing path.

This loop trusts the wrapped `size` from step 13 as the label bound. `off` therefore keeps advancing far beyond the real later-block bytes and continues walking through the backing honggfuzz input buffer until it reaches that buffer's end.

Sink. `md_decode_utf8__()` dereferences `str[0]` without validating that the pointer still lies inside the original input allocation. After step 15 has advanced the hash walker to the end of honggfuzz's 1048576-byte input buffer, this read hits the first byte past that region and ASan reports the observed heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 at `src/md4c.c:817`.

format.contract:
A `fuzz-mdhtml` testcase whose first 4 bytes set parser flags to `0xffffffff`, whose next 4 bytes set renderer flags to `0x2020ffff`, and whose exact 34-byte Markdown payload is `[][[![$|$]()]]

[\xff]:\xff
[[![|]()]][]`. On the vulnerable path, the first paragraph's wiki-link rollback leaves stale `TABLECELLBOUNDARIES` state that survives because the generic chain reset starts at index 2, and the later paragraph then reuses `ctx->marks` under that stale chain until `md_is_link_reference()` hashes a malformed single-line label with a wrapped unsigned `label_size`. The verified trigger is this exact staged witness shape, not a generalized class of all wiki-link inputs.
